full_judgment:
5. The Court of Settlement found on consideration of the materials on record that respondent No. 1 could not provide any date of death of original allottee, Md Yahiya save and except asserting that he died in 1970. Respondent No.1 could not also produce any certificate from anywhere relating to the death of Yahiya in 1970. The Court of Settlement also found that respondent No.1 could not produce any document in support of his contention that Md. Nasim was the only son and legal heir of the lessee Md Yahiya. The positive finding of the Court of Settlement was that there was no evidence that Yahiya died in 1970 in Bangladesh and Md. Nasim was his only heir. Apart from those above factual determinations, the Court of Settlement found that Respondent No. 1 could not rebut the presumption attached to the property that it is an abandoned property as per section 5(2) of Ordinance 54 of 1985 and found the house in question to be an abandoned house within the meaning of President's Order 16 of 1972. 

 8. It has been held by this Division in various decisions that the enlistment of a building under section 5(1) of Ordinance 54 of 1985 raises a presumption in law that the property is an abandoned property under section 5(2) of the Ordinance. This presumption is, of course, a rebuttable presumption but respondent No. 1 failed to rebut this presumption. No rebuttable evidence could be adduced to show that original owner Yahiya was present in Bangladesh and he occupied, managed or supervised the disputed building when President's Order 16 of 1972 came into operation. Hence, the listing of the property as an abandoned property in the Supplementary Provisions Ordinance, 1985 was lawful as it was an abandoned property by operation of law.
